body.title: Recover or rewrite the Initial Network Architecture
body.body:
## What is delivered
The Initial Network Architecture, published in this repository — or, if it cannot be consolidated from existing material, a first version written against the requirements that are published.

## Why it is needed
The README lists the network requirements and then says "Other requirements are specified in the Initial Network Architecture". That document is not published anywhere public, so the most consequential document of this layer is currently a reference to itself.

## Where to start
The published requirements are the contract: two networks, three layers, compatibility with Living Cryptography, modular and evolutionary protocol, intelligent interconnection, separation of layers and subnetworks, distribution and fault tolerance, offline adaptability, DFM architecture. A rewrite has to satisfy them, not replace them.

Recovering and consolidating what already exists is worth more than rewriting from scratch.
## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.title: The network carries the veto chain; English-only documentation
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: the network carries the veto chain; English only
- docs: the veto chain carries grounds and triage outcomes

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #3, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Carry one veto through a network partition
body.body:
## What is delivered
A small, reproducible experiment that carries one veto through a network partition, with the code or scripts and a short report.

The sequence: a veto is signed on a disconnected device; the network splits in two; the device reconnects to one side; the entry propagates and is checked by at least three independent nodes; the partition heals; an execution layer that was about to carry out the contested action refuses it once the entry arrives. Report what happened to ordering, duplicates and conflicting histories, and how long each step took.

## Why it is needed
The veto chain is only as strong as its behaviour under failure. "Replicated and accepted by propagation" is a claim until someone shows what a real partition does to it.

## Where to start
The section "Carrying the veto chain" in this repository's README and the veto chain in [UID](https://uid.drayker.org). Any small simulation or container setup is fine; the point is a result someone else can rerun.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn
